sections.h2: What probate law controls when a homeowner dies
sections.html:
Indiana's probate rules live in Title 29, Article 1 of the Indiana Code. They decide who can act for the estate, who inherits and how a house travels from the dead owner to a buyer. A relative who lives there or pays the bills has no power to sign a deed. Someone needs legal authority first.

That authority usually comes from a court appointment. Under IC 29-1-10-1, an executor named in a will comes first. With no will, the surviving spouse, or a person the spouse nominates, ranks ahead of the heirs, and the heirs follow. Minors and certain incapacitated people are disqualified wherever they rank.

The same code sets the deadlines a seller will run into: the claims period, the window to contest a will and the steps to close the estate. Those clocks shape how fast an inherited Indiana house can realistically change hands. Probate happens in the county where the case is opened, and the recorder in the county where the land sits receives any deed or recorded affidavit, even when the owner lived elsewhere.

sections.h2: Who inherits a house when there is no will?
sections.html:
When no valid will exists, IC 29-1-2-1 sends the estate to relatives in a set order, and the house follows everything else. The spouse and children come first, then parents, then siblings.

  • A surviving spouse with a child, or with a deceased child's descendants, takes one half of the net estate. The rest goes to the descendants, shared equally when they are in the same generation.
  • A spouse with no descendants but a living parent takes three fourths. With no descendants and no parent, the spouse takes everything.
  • A second or later spouse who has no children with the decedent, where the decedent left children from an earlier marriage, takes 25 percent of the real property's net fair market value, plus the usual share of personal property.
  • With no spouse and no descendants, the estate goes to surviving parents and to siblings and their descendants. Each parent counts as a sibling but receives at least one fourth.
  • If no relative in those groups survives, the statute works outward to grandparents, then the decedent's aunts and uncles and their descendants, and finally the state.

Co-heirs who inherit a house together each own a share. Any sale needs every owner to sign, so a missing or uncooperative heir can stall a closing for months.

A handful of dollar limits and time windows drive most decisions about an inherited house.

Deadline or limitRule
Small estate dollar limit (IC 29-1-8-1 and 29-1-8-3)$100,000 for deaths after June 30, 2022; $50,000 for deaths between mid-2006 and mid-2022; $25,000 before that
Wait before the personal property affidavit (IC 29-1-8-1)45 days after death (5 days for vehicles and watercraft)
Spouse or minor children allowance (IC 29-1-4-1)$25,000; election due within 90 days after the order opening administration
Creditor claims (IC 29-1-14-1)Barred after 3 months from first published notice, with a 9 month outer limit from death
Will contest (IC 29-1-7-17)3 months after the order admitting the will
Closing statement, unsupervised estate (IC 29-1-7.5-4)No earlier than 3 months after first published notice to creditors

The allowance deserves a second look. If the estate's personal property falls short of $25,000, the spouse or minor children can claim real estate for the difference, and the shortfall becomes a lien on the house. The real estate can be sold to satisfy it only with the consent of everyone interested, or by court order after notice.

sections.h2: Can a small estate affidavit transfer a house?
sections.html:
The affidavit in IC 29-1-8-1 is built for personal property, so it will not by itself put a deed in a buyer's hands. A distributee can collect bank balances, securities, insurance benefits, safe deposit contents and similar assets with it, and the Bureau of Motor Vehicles can retitle a car, once 45 days have gone by and no personal representative has been requested anywhere.

Real estate runs through IC 29-1-8-3. A fiduciary may distribute a qualifying estate without notice to creditors and then file a closing statement. If land is part of the estate, an affidavit may be recorded with the county recorder where the property sits. It needs the legal description, a statement that the estate is within the dollar limit, the name and share of each person entitled to an interest, and an explanation of how each share was worked out.

Recording is optional under the statute. Even so, buyers and title companies tend to want clear paper, so expect questions about who signed and on what authority.

sections.h2: How an unsupervised estate conveys a house
sections.html:
In an unsupervised estate, the personal representative can sell land without going back to the judge each time. IC 29-1-7.5-3 lets the representative dispose of an asset, land included, for cash or on credit at public or private sale, and to sell, mortgage or lease estate real property.

The paperwork is spelled out. The representative signs the deed, which can follow the statutory wording: it names the estate, the decedent, the cause number and the county, and it describes the real estate. Under IC 29-1-7.5-3.6, a conveyance in that form passes all title to the grantee. IC 29-1-7.5-3.4 gives a similar form for handing real property to a devisee or heir.

When the estate closes, the representative's closing statement must confirm that any real estate was conveyed by a recorded personal representative's deed. If no one starts a proceeding within three months after the statement is filed, the appointment ends and the estate closes by operation of law.

A recorded transfer on death deed is the main way an Indiana owner steers a house around probate. Under IC 32-17-14-11, the deed must be recorded with the county recorder before the owner dies, or it is void. It needs no consideration, no delivery and no auditor endorsement.

The type of ownership changes the effect:

  • Property held as tenants by the entirety stays out of reach unless the other spouse joins in the deed.
  • A joint tenancy with survivorship is severed and becomes a tenancy in common.
  • A life estate measured by the owner's life cannot be passed this way.

IC 32-21-1-15 adds a catch for later transfers. Once a transfer on death deed is on record, a later conveyance of the same property is void unless it was also recorded before the owner's death.

sections.h2: Where inherited house sales usually get stuck
sections.html:
Most delays come from authority, taxes and paperwork rather than the market. Indiana property tax for a given year is billed the following year in two installments, due May 10 and November 10 under IC 6-1.1-22-9, so an estate can open with a tax bill already waiting. A due date on a weekend moves to the next business day.

The deed itself passes through the county auditor and recorder. The auditor must endorse most deeds before the recorder accepts them, and a sales disclosure form is required with a transfer for value. Transfers from probate are among those exempt from the form's fee.

  • Heirs live in different states and need to coordinate signatures.
  • No one has opened an estate, so nobody can sign for the owner.
  • The house needs work, and the estate has no cash for repairs or insurance.
  • Creditor claims remain open until the claims period runs out.
  • A surviving spouse's allowance becomes a lien on the real estate.

Some families choose a cash sale to avoid carrying repair and holding costs while the estate works through these steps. A buyer paying cash can often close once the personal representative or the heirs can deliver a deed, though a title company decides what paperwork it needs for each file.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in Indiana?
faqs.a: There is no single timeline. Creditors have 3 months from the first published notice (with a 9 month cap from death), and an unsupervised representative can file a closing statement no earlier than 3 months after that notice. Contested wills, missing heirs and tax questions add time.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?
faqs.a: Yes, if the personal representative has authority. In an unsupervised estate the representative can sell land under IC 29-1-7.5-3 without a court order for each step. Without an appointment, no one can sign for the estate.

faqs.q: What is the small estate limit in 2026?
faqs.a: For deaths after June 30, 2022 it is $100,000, measured on the gross probate estate after liens, encumbrances and reasonable funeral expenses. IC 29-1-8-3 adds administration costs and funeral expenses to the threshold for the real property procedure.

faqs.q: Does a small estate affidavit let me sell a house?
faqs.a: The affidavit in IC 29-1-8-1 is for collecting personal property. For land, IC 29-1-8-3 lets an affidavit be recorded with the county recorder, but the distribution runs through a fiduciary, and a buyer's title company may ask for more.

faqs.q: Does a recorded transfer on death deed avoid probate?
faqs.a: For that parcel, yes, if it was recorded with the county recorder before the owner died. An unrecorded deed is void, and a tenancy by the entirety needs the other spouse to join.
